newsitem.title: USA: IPALCO to self-tender for 12 mln shares.
newsitem.headline: IPALCO to self-tender for 12 mln shares.

text.p: IPALCO Enterprises Inc said Tuesday its board approved a recapitalization plan involving a self-tender offer to buy up to 12 million or 21 percent of its outstanding shares.

It said the plan, which also calls for a lowering of the quarterly dividend to $0.25 per share from $0.37, is designed to maximize shareholder value. The tender offer, scheduled to begin February 28, will be through a "Dutch auction" at a price of not less than $29 and nor more than $34 per share.

IPALCO said the potential $410 million transaction will be financed with a five-year bank debt facility. The parent company recapitalization will not affect the capitalization of its wholly owned Indianapolis Power & Light Co subsidiary.
The $0.25 per share dividend will be paid on April 15 to holders of record March 21, regardless of whether the shares are tendered.
Future dividend action will be guided by, among other criteria, a policy of paying out 45 to 50 percent of the prior year's earnings, IPALCO said.
A targeted consolidalted debt-to-capital ratio of 45 percent which IPALCO said it believes can be achieved within the next five years.

John Hodowal, IPALCO chairman and president, said "With our solid underlying earnings prospects, combined with the effect of reduced shares outstanding, IPALCO is positioned to achieve strong growth in earnings per share in 1997. This will be further enhanced in 1998 and beyond as our cash flow enables the transaction debt to be repaid and interest expense to decline."
"By targeting a constant payout ratio, dividend growth in 1998 and subsequent years is positioned to be equally strong," he said.

Hodowal added, "We believe the price range established for our tender offer will allow those shareholders who desire a more income-oriented investment to exit their investment in IPALCO on favorable terms. However, we believe that shareholders who choose not to tender their shares also will benefit from this transaction. They will own a 26.7 percent greater interest in a highly competitive company with a stronger earnings per share growth rate," he said.
IPALCO's stock ended Tuesday up 1/8 at 28-1/8.

John Brehm, IPALCO's treasurer, summarized goals of the financial strategy by saying that they "will provide IPALCO with sufficient funds to replace existing assets and undertake investments in new growth, while maintaining a prudent balance between debt and equity in our capital structure."
The self-tender offer, the proration period and withdrawal rights will expire at midnight EST on March 27, unless extended.
IPALCO is a multi-state energy company providing a variety of energy related products and services.
